official.deadline_note: The deadline is the institutional approval and submission date in elane, not the date the applicant finishes: the lead Austrian research institution must approve and submit the application by 10 September 2026, 2:00 pm Vienna time, so individual institutions set earlier internal cut-offs. Late applications are returned without review regardless of circumstances.
official.application_cycle: 2026 call - application window 1 July 2026 to 10 September 2026; awards decided and formally announced in June the following year
official.status_note: The official programme page listed submissions for the 2026 round as 'July 1, 2026 to Sep. 10, 2026 (02:00 pm Vienna local time)' and on 2026-10-10 shows 'Currently no submissions'; the next call window is not yet published. The formal announcement of the FWF ASTRA Awards takes place in June.
benefits: Project-specific costs of at least EUR 500,000 up to a maximum of EUR 1 million for a period of five years

An additional EUR 200,000 tenure package for women ASTRA principal investigators granted a position with a permanent employment commitment upon fulfillment of a qualification agreement (e.g. tenure-track position) or a permanent academic leadership position within the first three years of the project term

Child allowance of EUR 9,600 per child per year (gross, paid in 12 monthly installments) for women principal investigators employed full-time after the birth of a child, up to the child's third birthday
Costs for personal coaching and/or personnel development measures for the principal investigator in the amount of up to EUR 10,000
Merit Award fallback: shortlisted projects presented at the hearing that do not receive an ASTRA Award are funded as three-year Principal Investigator Projects with a maximum of EUR 450,000 each
eligibility: Applicants must have a doctoral degree awarded at least 2 and not more than 9 years prior to September 30 of the year of submission, calculated from the date of the successful thesis defense exam (or official dissertation acceptance); exceptions such as parental leave are defined in the Application Guidelines
In arts-based research, researchers without a doctoral degree may apply with proof of at least 2 to a maximum of 9 years of relevant experience according to international standards
Individuals who already hold a tenured professorship or an equivalent permanent leadership position, or who have already accepted an appointment to such a position, are not eligible to apply
Researchers may apply to the ASTRA programme a maximum of two times throughout their career and may serve as principal investigator in only one approved project

All Austrian research institutions are eligible to apply; the project must be carried out in Austria under the auspices of the applying Austrian research institution, and the principal investigator must be employed at the lead research institution to an extent of at least 5 hours/week for the entire project duration

Researchers whose main institutional research focus (more than 50%) is outside Austria at the time of application, and who plan to maintain it abroad, are excluded from applying as principal investigators
requirements: Applications must be submitted online using the elane digital application portal and must be approved for submission by both the applicant and the lead research institution (PROFI mode)
Applications must be submitted in English so that they can be reviewed by international peers and the international jury

The project description may not exceed 20 pages (including table of contents, abbreviations, figures, tables and footnotes) and must follow the formatting rules: 11 pt font, 15-20 pt line spacing, at least 2 cm margins

The applicant's publication record over the last five calendar years must be internationally visible and commensurate with the expected career path, including at least two quality-assured and internationally visible publications with a substantial and independent contribution, at least one with first, last, or corresponding authorship

Parallel submissions to any of the FWF career programmes (ASTRA, Erwin Schroedinger, or ESPRIT) are prohibited, as are multiple funding and the parallel submission of a substantially identical application to other FWF programmes
The number of ASTRA applications per research institution should be limited in line with the Guidelines on the Maximum Number of ASTRA Applications
documents: Proposal.pdf: project description (max. 20 pages) including Annexes 1-4 with PDF bookmarks for the major sections
PI-publication.pdf: two publications written by the applicant documenting that the applicant fulfills the general requirements to apply
Publication_list.pdf: list of the applicant's publications over the last five calendar years, categorized into quality-assured and other publications
Alternative_project_plan.pdf: description including a cost breakdown of which parts of the ASTRA project will be conducted in the event of Merit Award funding

Online forms: Research institution assignment, Contact, Application, Program-specific data, Cost breakdown, Academic abstract (in English), Co-authors, plus Associated research partners and Other cooperation where applicable
Optional uploads: Cover_letter.pdf, Negative_list.pdf, Follow.pdf, Overview_revision.pdf and Revision.pdf for resubmissions
selection_criteria: Two-stage process: international peer review of all applications, followed by a shortlist drawn up by the FWF Scientific Board and a mandatory hearing before an international jury
The FWF Scientific Board decides on the award-winning proposals based on the jury's recommendations made after considering the results of the hearings

At least half of the FWF ASTRA Awards are granted to women; if the jury does not recommend a sufficient number of eligible women researchers, the FWF awards a correspondingly smaller number of grants to ensure the 50% minimum share

Projects presented at the hearing that do not receive an ASTRA Award are funded as three-year Principal Investigator Projects with a maximum of EUR 450,000 each (Merit Awards) if the alternative project plan is deemed plausible
coverage: Personnel and non-personnel costs needed to carry out the project that are not included in the infrastructure provided by the research institution

Eligible cost categories: personnel costs, equipment costs, material costs (items under EUR 1,500 incl. VAT), project-specific travel and accommodation, field work and expeditions, presentation of project results at conferences, costs of national and international collaborations, and publication costs
The FWF does not finance the infrastructure or basic equipment of research institutions

The principal investigator's salary is financed either by the research institution or by the project as a grant-salaried researcher; if the PI is employed part-time at the start of the project, project funds can be used to increase the extent of employment to 100%
Additional project funding of EUR 200,000 (tenure package) and EUR 9,600 per child per year (child allowance) are paid out as additional funding after approval
application_method: Online application through the elane digital application portal during the published application window
Completion of all required online forms and upload of all documents in full before the lead research institution approves the application for submission
Institutional approval and submission in elane by the deadline of 10 September 2026, 2:00 pm local time Vienna
official.application_route: Apply online via the FWF elane portal during the annual call window and have the lead Austrian research institution approve and submit the application before the deadline (PROFI mode).
official.citizenship_residency: No Austrian citizenship or residency requirement is published; the project must be carried out in Austria under the auspices of an Austrian research institution, the PI must be employed at the lead institution for at least 5 hours/week, and the programme may not be led from abroad.
official.international_eligibility: Open to successful, internationally visible researchers from all disciplines regardless of nationality, as long as the project is carried out at an Austrian research institution; researchers whose main institutional research focus (more than 50%) is outside Austria are excluded from applying as principal investigators.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open topic: open to researchers from all basic research disciplines, including arts-based research; no subject or agency restriction.
official.research_requirement: An original research project proposal in English of at most 20 pages with annexes, plus evidence of an internationally visible, independent publication record over the last five calendar years.
official.duration: Five years (Merit Award fallback: three years)
official.description: Attracting and retaining particularly talented researchers in international competition, the FWF ASTRA Awards give advanced postdocs in Austria the opportunity to make the leap to the top of their research field. The highly endowed awards offer outstanding researchers the conditions they need to conduct long-term research projects at a top international level, consolidate their individual research profiles, and acquire the necessary qualifications for academic leadership positions. The programme includes a number of measures for the advancement of women, and half of the awards are granted to women.
official.program_type: Career funding programme for advanced postdocs (R3-level principal investigator project)
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English to allow review by international peers and the international jury; no English language test (IELTS/TOEFL) is published.

tuition_coverage (no tuition statement published for this programme)

verification.notes: Amounts (EUR 500,000-1 million over five years, EUR 200,000 tenure package, EUR 450,000 Merit Award, EUR 9,600 child allowance, EUR 10,000 coaching) and the 10 September 2026 deadline were taken from the official FWF programme page and the Application Guidelines for the FWF ASTRA Awards (effective 1 July 2026) on fwf.ac.at.

applicant_utility.summary: ASTRA is not a personal scholarship but a five-year project grant of at least EUR 500,000 that you can only win if an Austrian research institution agrees to host you and approves your file in elane by the 10 September 2026, 2:00 pm Vienna deadline - so your first move is to secure that host and its internal sign-off, which typically falls weeks earlier. Eligibility hinges on your doctorate date being 2-9 years before 30 September of the submission year and on a publication record with at least two quality-assured, internationally visible outputs including one first, last, or corresponding authorship. Because half of the grants are reserved for women and the decision needs a mandatory jury hearing, even a shortlist place converts into EUR 450,000 of Merit Award funding, which gives unsuccessful finalists a second attempt.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Postdocs 2-9 years past their doctorate with an internationally visible publication record, competitive third-party funding or research time abroad, who want a large five-year project to build a professorship case at an Austrian institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your thesis defense date falls 2-9 years before 30 September of the submission year, and document any parental leave or career break using the FWF career-break information and checklist

Agree the project, budget and cost breakdown with your lead Austrian research institution early and ask for its internal deadline, since institutional approval in elane is the actual submission trigger

Verify you have at least two quality-assured, internationally visible publications with substantial independent contributions, one with first, last, or corresponding authorship, and list all outputs from the last five calendar years split into quality-assured and other publications
Draft the project description in English within the 20-page limit at 11 pt font, 15-20 pt line spacing and 2 cm margins, with annexes and PDF bookmarks

Budget personnel, equipment, materials (under EUR 1,500 per item), travel with a detailed itinerary per staff member, publication costs, and any associated research partners at other Austrian institutions
Prepare the Alternative project plan with its own cost breakdown, since Merit Award eligibility depends on this file being judged plausible
common_rejection_risks: Institutional approval missing at the 2:00 pm Vienna cutoff on 10 September 2026: late files are returned without review, with no exceptions
Holding or having already accepted a permanent professorship or equivalent leadership position, or having your main research focus (over 50%) outside Austria, which excludes you outright
A publication record that is nationally rather than internationally visible, or fewer than two quality-assured publications with a first/last/corresponding authorship
Parallel submissions to other FWF career programmes (ASTRA, Erwin Schroedinger, ESPRIT), multiple funding, or overlapping substantially with an already approved or ongoing FWF project
Exceeding your institution's recommended application cap, which can sink an otherwise strong file before peer review starts
A project description over 20 pages or failing the formatting rules, which invites formal return without review
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The principal investigator's own salary is financed either by the host institution or from project funds as a grant-salaried researcher, and the FWF explicitly does not finance institutional infrastructure or basic equipment, so any facility overhead, equipment the institution will not provide, and personal relocation or living costs must be covered by you or the host institution.
document_audit: Proposal.pdf needs PDF bookmarks at least for the major sections, and Annexes 1-4 must be inside the same 20-page envelope with the same font and margin rules
PI-publication.pdf must name exactly two publications that prove the general application requirements, not your best-known papers
The Co-authors form must briefly describe any AI tools used in preparing the proposal - omission is an easy formal defect

The publication list must be categorized into quality-assured and other publications; for journals not in Web of Science, Scopus or DOAJ you must supply a publisher link describing the quality assurance procedure
If you are claiming a career break, the information sheet, checklist and form for accounting for career breaks must all be uploaded or the eligibility window cannot be adjusted
alerts: As of 2026-10-10 the official page shows 'Currently no submissions': the 2026 window ran 1 July to 10 September 2026 and has closed, and the next call date is not yet published - historically the call has opened in mid-July to early July and the awards are announced the following June
The deadline is the institution's approval timestamp in elane, not your final edit, so internal host cut-offs decide your real timeline
You can apply to ASTRA only twice in your career and can be PI on only one approved project, and only one Merit Award can be awarded per researcher

The EUR 200,000 tenure package and the child allowance are conditional add-ons that require a permanent or tenure-track commitment within the first three years, or full-time employment after a birth, so they cannot be counted on at application time
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: You prepare the English proposal, annexes, publication files and online forms in elane, your lead research institution reviews and approves the submission before the 2:00 pm Vienna cutoff, and the FWF Office then formally checks every file before international peer review begins.
